source-e6350de0796d4044.content:
{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=socio-cognitive+architecture+collective+intelligence+AI+memory+attention+reasoning&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.31234/osf.io/4sqfx_v1\", \"title\": [\"The Structure of Collective Intelligence: Evidence for Collective Memory, Attention, and Reasoning\"], \"abstract\": \"

The ability for groups to effectively collaborate is important for both economic and societal progress. Extant research has demonstrated that group performance can be explained by a general \\\"collective intelligence\\\" (CI) factor, but there is ongoing debate about the components of CI with important implications for our understanding of how it develops or can be enhanced. We conduct a meta-analysis with data from 22 studies and 5,279 individuals in 1,356 groups to investigate the structure of collective intelligence using factor analysis. Our analysis yields strong support for a hierarchical three-factor model, supporting a theory that collective intelligence emerges from collective memory, attention, and reasoning. The model explains the data better than other plausible alternatives, especially in established groups who had the opportunity to develop their collective cognition over time. Our findings provide new insights into the formation of collective intelligence and have important implications for the design and evaluation of interventions that aim to increase it.

\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/4sqfx_v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 11, 27]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.4018/979-8-3373-8988-2.ch007\", \"title\": [\"Attention, Memory, Reasoning, Judgment, and Metacognitive Control in AI-Based Educational Decisions\"], \"abstract\": \"This chapter advances a conceptual-theoretical framework of brain-inspired Decision Intelligence for education, reframing AI not as prediction machinery but as a governance-gated socio-technical control system operating under partial observability, path dependence, and high-rights constraints. It synthesizes attentional gating, governed episodic-semantic-procedural memory, constraint-aware and causal-leaning reasoning, multi-objective judgment under harm asymmetry, and metacognitive control via calibrated uncertainty, selective prediction, abstention, and escalation. Hybrid architectures are specified across retrieval-centric, neuro-symbolic, causal planning, and human-AI teaming paradigms, coupled to procedurally defensible reasons-giving, contestability, and lifecycle accountability. The chapter delivers design constitutions through five tables, operationalizing admissible evidence, salience ethics, anti-stigma retrieval, bounded adaptation, and audit-ready due process for globally deployable, rights-compatible educational decision systems.\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.4018/979-8-3373-8988-2.ch007\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 8, 7]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.62891/7062086f\", \"title\": [\"AGI Submission Doc Toward a Modular Cognitive Architecture for Collective Intelligence: A P2P Platform for Distributed Epistemology, Semantic Processing, and Scalable Memory\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.62891/7062086f\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 5, 6]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.5921682\", \"title\": [\"The Cognitive Organization of Hybrid Intelligence: A Sociotechnical Architecture for Human-AI Co-Reasoning\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5921682\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "b6285878734a51f41baa58ea2c5929251e769a2fe6a2c72ea81f20becb4c6441"}

nb-ci-structure-evidence.findings: An editorial in the journal Collective Intelligence [source-b953b67b76fe4915] outlines a conceptual framework proposing that AI can support and augment a group's collective intelligence across three socio-cognitive elements: collective memory, collective attention, and collective reasoning. This tripartite taxonomy is supported empirically by a meta-analysis of 22 studies containing 5,279 individuals across 1,356 groups [source-e6350de0796d4044]. The meta-analysis yields strong support for a hierarchical three-factor model corresponding precisely to collective memory, collective attention, and collective reasoning. This structure fit the data better than other plausible alternatives, notably showing stronger statistical alignment in established groups that had time to develop collective cognition.
nb-ci-structure-evidence.limitations: Both sources are analyzed strictly from their provided metadata and abstracts; the full texts of the editorial and meta-analysis were not examined. The meta-analysis abstract notes that the hierarchical three-factor model fits better for 'established groups', indicating that the emergence of these distinct structural dimensions may be dependent on temporal group development and may not apply equally to ad-hoc teams.
nb-ci-structure-evidence.next_questions: How do specific artificial agents dynamically interface with these three channels? What specific protocols govern episodic memory versus causal reasoning in joint human-machine systems?
nb-ci-structure-evidence.reason: Synthesizes the first empirical meta-analysis of collective intelligence factors with the editorial conceptual framework, fulfilling the active research commitment.
nb-ci-structure-evidence.summary: We analyze how the conceptual framework of collective memory, attention, and reasoning as dimensions of collective intelligence aligns with recent hierarchical factor-analytic meta-analysis.
nb-ci-structure-evidence.title: Empirical Evidence for the Tripartite Structure of Collective Intelligence
